clue.text: Little brother should be carried

parts.note: BR is the short form of brother
should means ought, as in 'you ought to go'

explanation.surface: A small boy is told he deserves to be carried home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' tells you to shorten brother to its abbreviation BR.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past forms of verbs of transporting something held, as in a parcel conveyed by hand.

clue.text: A slow boat capsized by border

indicators.note: a boat that capsizes turns upside down, so in a down clue the word for the boat is read bottom to top

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

explanation.surface: A sluggish vessel turns over beside the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' suits a down clue: the boat word turns upside down, read bottom to top; 'by' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To border land is to lie next to it, touching its edge.

clue.text: Doesn't become badly affected by alcohol

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the preceding word are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that something will not turn out well when drink is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges DOESNT; the apostrophe is not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for heavily intoxicated, by drink or drugs.

clue.text: Secretary returned with little relish

indicators.note: returned means the short word for a secretary is sent back, read from the bottom up

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
petite means small

explanation.surface: An office assistant comes back with a small portion of a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns PA into AP; 'relish' looks like a condiment but means hunger or zest.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish as eagerness or keen desire for something, food especially.

clue.text: Cantankerous chap has to mend diagonally

parts.note: something lying crosswise runs diagonally, so cross can stand for it
to patch is to mend a hole

explanation.surface: A grumpy man is obliged to repair something on the slant.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumpy, irritable person; the old word for a bad-tempered sort.

clue.text: Is never wantonly contrary

indicators.note: wantonly means recklessly, without restraint, so the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who is never recklessly opposed to anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wantonly' rearranges ISNEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverse as an adjective means opposite in order or effect.

clue.text: Steal in sympathy, despite integrity

indicators.note: in tells you the word for steal is placed inside the word for sympathy

parts.note: pity is sympathy for someone's suffering
to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: Stealing out of compassion, yet with honour intact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'despite' is only a link; 'Steal' looks like the definition but supplies the inner piece, with 'in' as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Probity is uprightness and honesty of character.

clue.text: Bound to go without article if being economical

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for bound goes around the article

parts.note: a bound is a spring or leap
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to do without a newspaper item to save money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: SPRING wraps around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frugal, using little; a gerund matching the adjectival sense of thrifty.

clue.text: Committee receives request for tournament

parts.note: a petition is a formal request

explanation.surface: A committee takes in a request about a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives' is read as a link meaning gets: COM followed by PETITION.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a contest in which players vie to win.

clue.text: What the ancient mariner did to get the wedding guest's spray

definitions.text: What the ancient mariner did to get the wedding guest's spray

parts.words: What the ancient mariner did to get the wedding guest's spray
parts.note: in Coleridge's poem the Mariner detains a wedding guest to tell his tale, which names a verb for accosting someone; that word is also the flower spray a wedding guest wears

explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner opens with the Mariner stopping a guest on his way to a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means waylaying someone to talk; the noun is a flower worn in a lapel slit.

clue.text: The woman had to take off

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
'd is the contracted form of had, as in she'd

explanation.surface: A woman was obliged to depart.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'The woman had' as SHE'D, apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to cast off, as a snake its skin.

clue.text: Humiliated after having arrived

explanation.surface: Someone is embarrassed once they turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Showed up means embarrassed someone by outdoing them, and also appeared or turned up somewhere.

clue.text: Staff endlessly served out strudel, despite itchy feet

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for staff loses its final letter

parts.note: a wand is a staff or rod

indicators.note: served out suggests the pastry is dished up in pieces, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pastry handed round despite restless feet among the diners.
explanation.walkthrough: WAND loses its D to give WAN; 'served out' rearranges STRUDEL into DERLUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchy feet is an idiom for a restless urge to travel.

clue.text: Tax one male with a job

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A man with employment is charged a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: An impost is a levy or duty imposed by authority.

clue.text: They should show interest in clerical garb

parts.note: taken as written
vestments are the robes worn by clergy

explanation.surface: Priests in robes look attentive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show interest' looks like paying attention, but means earning interest on money.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks and deposits are expected to yield a financial return.

clue.text: I bumped in Ralph Waldo coming out

indicators.note: bumped in means pushed into, so the letter goes inside the surname

parts.note: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American essayist

explanation.surface: Someone collides with the American poet as he emerges.
explanation.walkthrough: Ralph Waldo Emerson, the 19th-century American essayist; I goes into EMERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Emersion is the act of emerging, as from water.

clue.text: Country people bursting into song

indicators.note: bursting into means forcing a way inside, so the word for people goes within the word for song

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera
men are people

explanation.surface: A crowd suddenly starts singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursting into song' reads as a stock phrase about singing, but 'bursting into' is the container signal and 'song' a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a nation in the Caucasus.

clue.text: Infuriated by a change of gender

indicators.note: change of means the word that follows has its letters altered in order

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a gender reassignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' looks like part of a phrase about gender, but it signals a rearrangement of that word, kept after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean made extremely cross.

clue.text: Flourishing English novelist

parts.note: green means growing and vigorous

explanation.surface: A thriving English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Graham Greene wrote Brighton Rock and The Power and the Glory.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was a celebrated British writer of fiction.

clue.text: Article about each child initially offered instruction

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for article is placed around the rest

parts.note: an article is an object, a thing

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on how every child was first given lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' tempts you to A, AN or THE, but here it is an object; 'about' wraps it round the rest, and 'offered' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching is the giving of lessons or tuition.

clue.text: Splendid child with love for martial art

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as I
a kid is a child
O is love, zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A gifted youngster with a passion for combat sport.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means excellent; its 1 stands in for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikido is a Japanese style of self-defence.

clue.text: Unpopular doctor lost his standing

explanation.surface: A disliked physician falls from grace.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'I do not like thee, Doctor Fell' makes the doctor a byword for someone disliked without reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Fell is the subject of a rhyme about inexplicable dislike, and to have toppled over is to lose one's footing.

clue.text: His business is to inform on zoo attendant

parts.note: to shop someone is slang for informing on them to the police
a keeper looks after animals at a zoo

explanation.surface: A man whose job is to betray an animal keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His business' points to a person who runs a business; 'shop' as informing is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer is a man whose living is his trading premises.

clue.text: Muslim leader in semi-retirement

indicators.note: in tells you the answer lies within the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: An Islamic ruler is partly stepping down.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a ruler or commander in Islamic lands.

clue.text: The man who conquers with style

parts.note: wins means triumphs or conquers
ton means fashionable style

explanation.surface: Someone who wins in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The man' points to a man's name, Churchill's first name perhaps; 'who' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston is a man's given name, borne by Churchill.

clue.text: Suitor is married, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters fall into a different order

explanation.surface: A man courting a woman discovers she already has a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges MARRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is someone who courts or woos a person.
